newsitem.title: UK: US stocks mostly firmer in London, Intel eases.
newsitem.headline: US stocks mostly firmer in London, Intel eases.

text.p: Most U.S. stocks were firmer in London on Tuesday, although shares in Intel Corp, the day's main feature, stumbled, dealers said.

Intel shares were trading $3 lower at $130-3/4 in London, erasing most of Monday's gains in New York, after the semiconductor giant warned that its second quarter revenues could be flat to only slightly higher.
The company, the world's biggest computer chip maker, made the statement after posting much stronger-than-expected first quarter earnings after New York markets closed.
Shares in Texas Instruments Inc eased $3/4 to $82-1/8 amid doubts the company's earnings will meet analysts' expectations, London dealers said.
Texas Instruments is due to report its first quarter results today.
Among other technology stocks, shares in International Business Machines Corp added $1/4 to $136-7/8. Shares in Digital Equipment Corp added $1/4 in London to $26-1/4.

"Just about everything is trading around $1/4 above their New York close. The market could continue higher, but it all will depend on the CPI," a dealer said. "The market is still nervous. (S&P 500) futures look shaky."
June S&P 500 index futures were off 1.25 point to 746.05 on Globex at 1034 GMT. June long bond futures were up 3/32 to 106-25/32.
The consumer price index for March, due at 1230 GMT, is expected to show prices rose 0.2 percent. Excluding the volatile food and energy component, the index is seen up 0.3 percent.
A rise much larger than that would heighten expectations the Federal Reserve will tighten credit more aggressively to ward off inflation.
Business inventories for February also will be released at 1230 GMT.

In other trading in London, shares in Citicorp were down $1/2 to $106 ahead of its first quarter results. But volume was light and dealers said they doubted the decline was not indicative of market sentiment.
Shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc were trading $1/8 higher to $38-1/2 in thin dealings.
Shares in Ford Motor Co were up $1/8 to $32-5/8, while shares in General Motors Corp, which released its first quarter earnings on Monday, were up $1/8 to $53-3/4.
